clue.text: Weapon a touch in fashion

indicators.note: the phrase 'a touch' is set in the middle of the word for fashion

parts.note: a cult is a craze or fashion
a tap is a light touch

explanation.surface: A trendy weapon described as being a touch in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is a device for hurling stones or missiles, an old weapon.

clue.text: Kept in attic, a feculent greasy spoon, perhaps

indicators.note: the answer is kept inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Something stored in a filthy attic, described as a grubby eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: A greasy spoon is British slang for a cheap, basic café serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is one example of a cheap eatery, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Tramp beating up pirates

indicators.note: a beating up knocks the pirates' letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A vagrant attacking some pirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' reads as a noun, a vagrant, but the definition is the verb, to trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily and wearily, a synonym of trudging along.

clue.text: Show capital in Paris, France more exotic

indicators.note: the capital, or initial letter, of the word Paris is taken
something exotic is strange and unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A show in the French capital, with France seeming more exotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital in Paris' tempts the solver to think of a city, but it is the capital letter of Paris. 'more' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is a show staged in front of an audience; they are synonyms.

clue.text: African introduced to Swahili by a nomad

indicators.note: the answer is introduced inside the letters of these words, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: An African nomad teaching someone Swahili.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Libya, a North African country, is an African by nationality.

clue.text: Cry when tulip, say, knocked over

indicators.note: a thing knocked over is upended, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tulip is an example of a bulb

explanation.surface: Someone crying because their tulip was knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is just a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is informal British slang for weeping or sobbing.

clue.text: Member beginning to overcome period of uncertainty

parts.note: an arm or leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A club member starting to overcome a phase of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means waiting in an unresolved, uncertain state.

clue.text: Railing is in raillery!

indicators.note: the word 'is' is placed inside the synonym for raillery

parts.note: raillery is good-humoured teasing, or banter

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the word railing appears inside raillery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests RAILING is spelt within RAILLERY, which almost works; the exclamation mark flags the playful trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up a staircase, a kind of railing.

clue.text: Learner surrounded by mediocre talent

indicators.note: the learner's letter sits with the word for mediocre around it

parts.note: fair can mean middling or only average
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A trainee with only average ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A flair for something is a natural aptitude or gift for it.

clue.text: Superhero imprisoning last of villains: he doesn't want to get out

definitions.text: he doesn't want to get out

indicators.note: the superhero holds the letter inside himself, as if jailing it

parts.note: Batman is the caped comic-book superhero

indicators.note: the final letter of the word villains is taken

explanation.surface: Batman locking up villains who would rather stay out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the batsman is the player batting, who tries not to be dismissed ('out'); the surface makes 'get out' sound like escaping prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket hitter's aim is to stay in and avoid dismissal, cryptically described.

clue.text: Drunken flirtatious gestures perhaps, a game

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
winks are an example of a flirtatious gesture

explanation.surface: A tipsy person winking flirtatiously during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a children's game of flicking small counters into a cup.

clue.text: Those for and against, experts and criminals

definitions.meaning: professionals plus convicts, each in short form

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means advantages and disadvantages, and also reads literally as professionals with convicts.

clue.text: Mincing of sausages is satisfying

indicators.note: mincing chops up the sausages, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making minced sausages is a pleasing task.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage hunger or a desire is to satisfy or relieve it.

clue.text: Unfortunately, my seat is hot

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome has things going awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's chair has become too warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy means hot and humid, full of vapour, so it fits hot.

clue.text: Promise to put shelf behind piano

indicators.note: the shelf word is put after, so behind, the piano letter

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Vowing to install a shelf behind the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn vow or undertaking, the same as a promise.

clue.text: Pick out loose cinders

indicators.note: loose cinders are scattered, so their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Sorting through scattered cinders from a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to make out or distinguish, to pick something out.

clue.text: Stick notice on this crossword?

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a public notice
on this very puzzle is right here

explanation.surface: A suggestion to glue a notice onto this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay attached, a synonym of the verb stick.

clue.text: Good times and bad — a lift attendant's experiences?

definitions.meaning: fluctuations of fortune, the highs and lows of life
someone operating an elevator literally spends the day rising and descending

explanation.surface: A lift operator reflecting on the highs and lows of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a literal-minded pun: an elevator goes up and down all day.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means alternating spells of success and failure in life.

clue.text: Very fast boy I caught

parts.note: a son is a boy child
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A speedy lad boasting that he took a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic relates to the speed of sound, so it describes something extremely quick.

clue.text: Spring, effectively

definitions.meaning: a natural source of water from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A well is a water source like a spring, and the adverb means competently or effectively.

clue.text: No tucking into fatty birds from Italy

indicators.note: the word no tucks itself inside the birds' name

explanation.surface: Declining to eat fatty Italian poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese means coming from Genoa, a city in Italy, so a narrower sense of Italian.

clue.text: Auntie finally hugged by lovely relative

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the word for lovely, as in an embrace
the final letter of the word Auntie is taken

explanation.surface: An aunt being cuddled by a lovely family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member or relation.

clue.text: Fire container

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from a job
a large bag for holding goods

explanation.definitionFit: To sack a worker is to dismiss them, and a sack is a big bag for storage.

clue.text: Private planes or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Choosing private jets or some other option.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal matters are private ones, belonging to an individual alone.
